mechanism_narrative: The sharp simultaneous drop in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RETAIL_REC at t-0w indicates a new restriction or avoidance shock. If that shock persists, retail visits should remain below the prior four-week average over the next month because lower commuting and footfall reduce incidental shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 and WORKPLACES falls below -10 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean for two consecutive weeks despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES staying below -10.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remain elevated while RETAIL_REC falls, households are substituting toward home-based activity and essential-only trips. That pattern should keep discretionary retail mobility weak over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above 0 and RESIDENTIAL is above 3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC returns to at least its pre-shock weekly average while GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL stay elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in PARKS and TRANSIT after an earlier park surge signals broad reductions in out-of-home activity, which should spill into weaker retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when both categories move down together rather than one offsetting the other.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean even though PARKS and TRANSIT both remain negative for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops abruptly by more than 10 points week-on-week, the mobility shock should transmit into RETAIL_REC within one week through reduced access to commercial districts. This is a short-lag mechanism that should show an immediate retail decline after transit collapse.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week of a TRANSIT drop greater than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in RESIDENTIAL while WORKPLACES weakens marks more time spent at home and fewer discretionary outings. That should keep RETAIL_REC below the prior month average over the next month because home-centric routines suppress shopping trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises for four consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above its recent peak and WORKPLACES remains below its previous average.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a short dip should precede a retail recovery only if outdoor leisure and shopping co-move. If PARKS turns back up from negative to positive within two weeks, retail mobility should improve modestly as leisure trips spill over into nearby stores.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from below 0 to above 0
failure_condition: PARKS turns positive but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling TRANSIT and rising RESIDENTIAL implies a commute substitution into home time, which should suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two to four weeks. The signal is stronger when the two series move in opposite directions in the same week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT falling and RESIDENTIAL rising in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both deeply negative, the city is likely in a mobility-restriction regime that should keep discretionary retail suppressed for the next month. Retail should only recover if both work attendance and transit usage normalize together.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -10 and TRANSIT falls below -10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean before WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover above -10.
